item.text:
I refactored the remaining duplication between the typed and legacy APIs.

[BellmanFord.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/BellmanFord.java:1) now has a typed raw-data overload, `computeShortestPaths(int vertices, int[][] edgeData, int source)`, so callers no longer have to choose between “typed result” and “raw edge input.” The legacy `shortestPaths(...)` path now delegates through that overload, and the internal success-path duplication was reduced by pushing result construction into `DistanceState.toResult()`.

I also refactored fixtures into scenario objects in [BellmanFordFixtures.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/BellmanFordFixtures.java:1). Each case now owns the graph, source, expected result, and raw edge export via [WeightedGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/WeightedGraph.java:1)`#edgeData()`. That removed the last duplicated graph definitions between the typed tests, legacy tests, and demo. [BellmanFordDemo.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/BellmanFordDemo.java:1) and [BellmanFordTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/BellmanFordTest.java:1) now run off the same shared cases, and the tests also cover the new raw typed overload.

Verification is clean: `javac *.java` succeeds, `java BellmanFordDemo` prints `ShortestPathResult{distances=[0, 5, 6, 6, 7], reachable=[true, true, true, true, true]}`, and `java BellmanFordTest` prints `All BellmanFord tests passed.`
